Commentary.Commentary: Back with the chase. Out walk the openers of India Women, where Shafali Verma will open the inning alongside Smriti Mandhana. Lauren Bell has the new ball in her hand and she will start the proceedings. Here we go...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, the match is now beautifully poised. A target of 172 runs is competitive but certainly chaseable on a good batting pitch like this, especially with the form India’s top order has shown recently. The momentum is with India after that dramatic collapse. On the flip side, England will be eager to regroup and come hard with the ball. They have quality bowlers who can exploit the conditions and apply pressure. A thrilling finish awaits, so don't go anywhere as the action for the second inning isn't far away!

But the tide turned swiftly. It all started with Deepti Sharma, who got the big breakthrough by dismissing the well-set Dunkley, and ended with three wickets overall. What followed was an avalanche. Arundhati Reddy triggered a collapse in the very next over, picking three wickets, including Wyatt-Hodge and Amy Jones in back-to-back balls. England's middle order fell apart with barely any resistance. Radha Yadav joined the party with a wicket, and Shree Charani cleaned up the lower order with two in two balls in the penultimate over. England’s batting card post the openers read like a horror script, as the next nine batters failed to cross double digits, except Sophie Ecclestone. What could’ve been a mammoth score ended in a rather modest finish.

The start from England was as clinical as it gets. Dunkley and Wyatt-Hodge were on cruise control from the word go. They negotiated the new ball smartly and began to accelerate after the Powerplay. Dunkley, in particular, was striking the ball sweetly and raced to her fifty, picking gaps at will and punishing anything remotely loose. Wyatt-Hodge was dropped twice early on, first by Jemimah Rodrigues and then by Harmanpreet Kaur in the same over, and she made India pay with a powerful 66 off just 42 balls. Their 137-run stand set the perfect platform for a 190-plus total, and at one stage, it looked like England would run away with the game.

England Women’s innings in the third T20I will go down in two contrasting halves. What began as a dominating batting performance soon spiralled into a chaotic collapse, handing India a golden opportunity to make a comeback in this must-win game for the hosts. After electing to bat first, England looked firmly in control with an opening stand of 137 runs between Sophia Dunkley and Danni Wyatt-Hodge. Dunkley looked fluent, composed, and untroubled, while Wyatt-Hodge managed to turn around a shaky start into something meaningful. However, the final five overs turned the entire script on its head as England crumbled from 137/0 to 171/9, losing 9 wickets for just 34 runs. The momentum has now firmly shifted towards India, who will walk into the chase with renewed energy and belief.

India Women (Unchanged Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Amanjot Kaur, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Radha Yadav, Arundhati Reddy, Sneh Rana, Shree Charani.

England Women (Playing XI) - Danni Wyatt-Hodge, Sophia Dunkley, Alice Capsey, Tammy Beaumont (C), Amy Jones (WK), Paige Scholfield (In for Nat Sciver-Brunt), Sophie Ecclestone, Issy Wong (In for Linsey Smith), Charlie Dean (In for Em Arlott), Lauren Filer, Lauren Bell.
TOSS - England Women have won the toss and they have elected to BAT first.

The weather at the Oval is expected to be partly warm, and the surface here traditionally plays true, but spinners will come into play as the match progresses. India’s strong spin attack might enjoy the conditions, while England need their experienced heads to step up. With momentum firmly with the visitors, England must dig deep and find answers fast. Stay tuned for the toss and team lineups!

England, however, are under pressure. Their batting unit has faltered in both matches, and the absence of Sciver-Brunt now leaves a massive void in both leadership and firepower. Tammy Beaumont looked sharp in the last game, but the rest of the top order has struggled to find the rhythm. On the bowling front, Lauren Bell has been excellent with the new ball, but there’s been a lack of support around her. If England are to stay alive in the series, they need a complete team effort and a much stronger batting show.

India’s campaign so far has been clinical. The bowlers have shown discipline and adaptability, with youngster Shree Charani continuing to impress with her control and breakthroughs. Jemimah has anchored the middle overs beautifully, while Amanjot has emerged as a dependable all-rounder, delivering with both bat and ball. Harmanpreet’s return added depth, even though she’s yet to find her groove. The visitors are high on confidence, with all departments functioning in sync and a clear hunger to seal the series.

The second T20I in Bristol saw India extend their dominance with a 24-run win. Despite losing their top order early, Jemimah Rodrigues and Amanjot Kaur stitched together a game-changing 93-run partnership. Amanjot remained unbeaten on 63, earning Player of the Match honours, while Richa Ghosh’s late cameo powered India to 181/4. In reply, England’s top order crumbled once again, losing three wickets inside four overs. Although Beaumont struck a fluent 54 and Ecclestone added a quick 35, the target proved too steep.

Hello and welcome to the iconic Oval in London for the third T20I between India Women and England Women. With two commanding wins, India stand on the brink of sealing the series, while England desperately search for answers. A win for the visitors here would wrap up the series with two games to spare, while England must respond strongly to keep the contest alive. The absence of Nat Sciver-Brunt due to injury adds to England’s woes, handing leadership duties to Tammy Beaumont and a huge responsibility to the rest of the squad.

The five-match T20I series between England Women and India Women heads to Kennington Oval, London, for a pivotal 3rd T20I. India Women currently hold a commanding 2-0 lead, having comprehensively beaten the hosts in the first two encounters. Another victory for India would seal a historic maiden T20I series triumph over England, a feat they have never achieved before. India Women have been in exceptional form, showcasing a well-rounded performance in both matches. In the series opener at Trent Bridge, they handed England a record-shattering 97-run defeat. This was largely thanks to a blistering maiden T20I century from stand-in captain Smriti Mandhana (112 off 62 balls), which propelled India to a formidable total of 210/5 – their highest ever T20I score against England. The second T20I in Bristol saw India continue their winning ways with a 24-run victory, which marked England Women's first-ever T20I loss at that venue. Despite an early wobble, dual half-centuries from Jemimah Rodrigues (63 off 41) and Amanjot Kaur (63 not out off 40) rescued India from 31/3 to post 181/4. The Indian bowling attack, even in the absence of pace spearheads Renuka Singh and Pooja Vastrakar, has stepped up admirably. Left-arm spinner Shree Charani has been the breakout star, leading the wicket charts with six scalps and boasting an impressive economy rate of 5.11 in her debut series. For England, this 3rd T20I is a do-or-die clash. A third consecutive loss would see them surrender the series with two games still to play. Their batting has struggled, particularly the opening pair of Sophia Dunkley and Danni Wyatt-Hodge, who have failed to provide solid starts. Wyatt-Hodge, in particular, has had a dismal summer, registering just 18 runs across five innings, including three successive ducks. Even new skipper Nat Sciver-Brunt has found it tough to get going. While players like Tammy Beaumont and Sophie Ecclestone have shown glimpses of form, consistency has been lacking. England's bowling, too, has been subpar, struggling to contain India's aggressive batting. Historically, England has held the upper hand in T20Is against India, with 22 wins to India's 9 in 31 encounters. However, India's recent performances suggest a shift in momentum. On home soil, England still has an advantage, but India's current form could override that. The pressure is undoubtedly on the home side to deliver a vastly improved performance. Who are you backing for the win?
